gaps.sentence: He ___ her on her excellent presentation.
gaps.explanation: 'Compliment somebody on something' means to praise; 'complement' means to go well with.

gaps.sentence: All ___ must wear identity badges at all times on site.
gaps.explanation: 'Personnel' = the employees of an organisation; 'personal' is an adjective.

gaps.sentence: You ___ a lot of water by having such long showers.
gaps.hint: to use something valuable without needing to
gaps.explanation: 'Waste' means to use more than necessary; 'save' means the opposite — to avoid using.

gaps.sentence: Thousands of people were forced to ___ their homes.
gaps.hint: a verb is needed after 'to'; meaning: abandon
gaps.explanation: 'Desert' is also a verb meaning to abandon; 'dessert' is only the sweet course of a meal.

gaps.sentence: Tax is calculated on your total annual ___.
gaps.hint: all the money you receive from every source
gaps.explanation: 'Income' is all the money you receive from work, investments, rent and so on during a period.

gaps.sentence: I start my new ___ at the hospital on Monday.
gaps.hint: a single, countable position of employment
gaps.explanation: 'Job' is countable — one particular position; 'work' is uncountable and cannot follow 'a new'.

gaps.sentence: The wine is the perfect ___ to the meal.
gaps.explanation: 'Complement' = something that completes or goes well with; 'compliment' is praise.

gaps.sentence: Pens, envelopes and paper are sold in the ___ department.
gaps.explanation: 'Stationery' means writing materials; 'stationary' is an adjective meaning not moving.
